key_insight: BrainG3N introduces a 3D brain MRI tokenizer that separates clinically useful embeddings from image reconstruction, enabling both strong downstream representation learning and controllable generation.
clinical_relevance: A single embedding space could help support clinical benchmarking, conditional brain MRI synthesis, and patient-specific longitudinal forecasting for neurology and neuro-oncology research.
method: Frozen 3D MAE encoder learns volumetric brain MRI embeddings
Dedicated CNN decoder reconstructs voxels from projected embeddings
Conditional diffusion transformer uses the embeddings for generation and forecasting
evidence_signal: Pretrained on 35,309 volumes from 18 public cohorts, the encoder matched or exceeded prior models on 21 of 23 linear-probing tasks and supported conditional generation across six variables.
watch_item: Promising results are based on retrospective public datasets, so generalization and safe use across sites, scanners, and clinical contexts still need careful validation.
paper_title: BrainG3N: A Dual-Purpose Tokenizer for Controllable 3D Brain MRI Generation
